k_{\max}= \inf_{a>0,\;b>0}\frac{(a+b)(ab+1)(b+1)}{ab^{2}} .
\]

---

### 1.  Reduce the number of variables  

Put  

\[
p=ab\qquad (p>0),\qquad  b=y\;(y>0)\ .
\]

Then \(a=\dfrac{p}{y}\) and  

\[
\frac{(a+b)(ab+1)(b+1)}{ab^{2}}
   =\frac{\bigl(\frac{p}{y}+y\bigr)(p+1)(y+1)}{p\,y}
   =\frac{(p+y^{2})(p+1)(y+1)}{p\,y^{2}} .
\]

Hence

\[
F(p,y)=\frac{(p+y^{2})(p+1)(y+1)}{p\,y^{2}}
      =\frac{y+1}{y^{2}}\Bigl(p+\frac{y^{2}}{p}+1+y^{2}\Bigr)
\qquad(p>0,\;y>0).
\]

---

### 2.  Minimising in \(p\) for a fixed \(y\)

For a fixed \(y\) the factor  

\[
g(p)=p+\frac{y^{2}}{p}
\]

is minimized by the AM–GM inequality:

\[
p+\frac{y^{2}}{p}\ge 2\sqrt{p\cdot \frac{y^{2}}{p}}=2y,
\]

with equality when \(p=y\).

Thus for each \(y\)

\[
F(p,y)\ge \frac{y+1}{y^{2}}\bigl(2y+1+y^{2}\bigr)
        =\frac{y+1}{y^{2}}(y+1)^{2}
        =\frac{(y+1)^{3}}{y^{2}} .
\]

The right–hand side depends only on \(y\).

---

### 3.  Minimise the one‑variable function  

Define  

\[
h(y)=\frac{(y+1)^{3}}{y^{2}},\qquad y>0.
\]

\[
\ln h(y)=3\ln(y+1)-2\ln y,\qquad 
\frac{d}{dy}\ln h(y)=\frac{3}{y+1}-\frac{2}{y}=0
\]

gives \(3y=2(y+1)\Rightarrow y=2\).

Since \(h''(y)>0\) for \(y>0\), \(y=2\) is the point of minimum.  

\[
h_{\min}=h(2)=\frac{(2+1)^{3}}{2^{2}}=\frac{27}{4}.
\]

---

### 4.  Value of \(k\)

The smallest possible value of the ratio is \(\displaystyle \frac{27}{4}\).  
Hence the inequality  

\[
(a+b)(ab+1)(b+1)\ge k\,ab^{2}\qquad (a,b>0)
\]

holds for all positive \(a,b\) precisely when  

\[
k\le\frac{27}{4}.
\]

Equality occurs for \(y=2\) (i.e. \(b=2\)) and \(p=y\) (i.e. \(ab=2\)), giving \(a=1\).
